advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix `_truncating_paged_search`'s no-op ternary (line 334) so it actually models the truncating behavior it documents, or simplify it to `return issues` and drop the misleading conditional/docstring.
evidence: tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_live_oracles_discriminate_5200.py:334: `    return issues if len(issues) >= 100 else issues`

Docstring at :327-330 claims it should 'advance by the REQUESTED size and stop on a short page' — but the body makes exactly one request and both ternary branches yield `issues`, so no advancing and no short-page stop is implemented.
Consumer at :371-374 relies on `via_subject < target` to prove the stand-in truncated; that only holds because `_ClampingSearch(total=201, clamp=50)` serves 50 < the requested 100.
advisory.finding: `_truncating_paged_search` has a dead conditional: `return issues if len(issues) >= 100 else issues` returns the identical value in both branches, so the function does NOT implement the 'advance by REQUESTED size and stop on a short page' truncation behavior its docstring claims. It only issues a single request and returns whatever the server served. It currently 'works' as a truncating stand-in solely because the clamp (50) is less than the requested page (100); if reused with clamp>=100 the stated truncation semantics silently would not hold, and the `via_subject < target` assertion in test_the_old_precondition_fails_on_the_very_defect_it_disclaimed would be a false comparison.
advisory.suggested_fix: Either simplify to `return issues` (a single short page is enough to show under-counting) and align the docstring, or genuinely model the historical bug by paging with `start_at += asked` and stopping on the first short page.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the production-source text greps in `test_the_writer_emits_the_COLON_label_form_and_nothing_emits_the_hyphen` with a behavioral assertion on the label an outbound create actually emits (e.g. drive the writer against a fake client and assert the captured `add_label` argument).
evidence: docstring admits: 'Asserted as source text because a label literal is a string, which is precisely the thing a semantic reference search cannot see.'

Refactoring violation: the grepped tokens are implementation strings in SOURCE CODE UNDER TEST (verified emitted at src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py:306, apply_inbound_records.py:290, binding_store.py:705), not tokens read by a non-human consumer, so Rule-5 structural-artifact exception does not apply.
advisory.finding: `test_the_writer_emits_the_COLON_label_form_and_nothing_emits_the_hyphen` asserts on the literal TEXT of production source files under test (`'f"rebar-id:{local_id}"' in source` and `'add_label(keyed, f"rebar-id-{local_id}")' not in source`) rather than on the label the writers actually emit. This is source-grepping of code under test: it breaks on a behavior-preserving refactor (extracting a `_rebar_label()` helper, renaming the local var) while the emitted label is unchanged, and the negative hyphen check only matches one exact call spelling so any other hyphen-write spelling passes silently.
scenarios: A maintainer extracts `f"rebar-id:{local_id}"` into a shared `_rebar_label(local_id)` helper: emitted behavior identical, but this test goes RED.
A regression writes the hyphen label via a differently-spelled call: the `not in source` check stays GREEN and misses it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Invoke the writer (or `assert_outbound_provenance_markers`) against a fake client capturing `add_label` calls and assert the captured label equals `rebar-id:<local_id>` and never the hyphen form, instead of reading and substring-matching the .py source text.
